profile.headline: Software Engineer | LLM systems & RAG in production | ex-BlackRock | Yale CS
profile.summary:
I work on making LLM systems accurate enough to trust in domains where a wrong answer has a legal consequence.

At CompliantRx I own accuracy evaluation end to end for the platform that reviews Medicare documentation for durable medical equipment claims. I built the evaluation pipeline from scratch in a day (ground-truth extraction from the legacy Azure system, batch execution against the new AWS Bedrock RAG pipeline, automated comparison), produced the first measured accuracy baseline the company had, and traced every failure to a specific stage: OCR, chunking, embedding, retrieval, generation, or the compliance logic sitting after all of it.

Most of what looked like "the model got it wrong" was not the model. The worst-performing criterion scored 21.9% at baseline, and the root cause turned out to be a date-comparison branch in post-processing. Correct retrieval, correct LLM output, overridden downstream.

That distinction is most of the job. Knowing whether an LLM system is failing at the model, the retrieval, or the code wrapped around it is what separates an evaluation that changes something from a dashboard nobody acts on.

Before this I spent two and a half years at BlackRock, in the COO org supporting Latin American institutional business. I built an end-to-end RAG assistant that answered client questions from internal documentation with grounded answers and source citations, LLM-assisted parsing to pull structured fields out of unstructured materials, and a reporting pipeline (ingest, compute, render, publish) that replaced manual and contractor steps and saved roughly $500K a year.

Outside work I build and maintain crisisvenezuela.org, an open damage-mapping platform for the 24 June 2026 Venezuela earthquakes. It aggregates testimony, official assessments, and media into a source-traceable register, published as an open dataset on Zenodo. The New Zealand Society for Earthquake Engineering routed its field triage data into it, and cites it in their reconnaissance report on the event.

Yale, BS in Computer Science and Economics. English and Spanish, both native.

positions.description:
Applied AI / accuracy engineering on the CRx Intelligence platform — LLM compliance review systems for durable medical equipment Medicare audits.

• Own end-to-end accuracy evaluation for a new AWS Bedrock RAG pipeline replacing a legacy OpenAI Assistants system; quantified baseline accuracy and traced failures across OCR, chunking, embeddings, retrieval, and generation stages
• Diagnose LLM failure patterns at both the prompt and architectural level; translate findings into measurable accuracy improvements
• Partner with clinical SMEs to convert domain-specific failure modes into systematic engineering fixes

Stack: Python, AWS Bedrock, RAG, embeddings, prompt engineering, LLM evaluation, FastAPI, PostgreSQL

• Designed reporting pipelines (ingest, compute, render, publish) with validation, fallbacks, and routing logic
• Developed reusable portfolio analytics modules

projects.title: crisisvenezuela.org
projects.description: Built and maintain an open damage-mapping platform for the 24 June 2026 Venezuela earthquakes (M7.2 + M7.5). Aggregates testimony, official assessments, and media into a source-traceable register used by reconnaissance teams, with a fail-closed trust model: every public record carries its evidence and confidence. The published NZSEE reconnaissance report names the platform (p.3), and the StEER Preliminary Virtual Reconnaissance Report includes a named acknowledgment (p.6) and formal reference (p.84): doi.org/10.17603/ds2-yd90-gt80. Dataset: doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21154222

publications.title: crisisvenezuela.org building-damage dataset, Venezuela earthquakes of 24 June 2026
